scenes.heading: Embeddings & Semantic Similarity
scenes.narration: Let's look at embeddings — the trick that lets a computer compare the meaning of two texts as a number.

scenes.heading: Turning meaning into math
items: An embedding model maps text to a vector
Similar meaning lands nearby in the space
Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors
'car' and 'automobile' score high with no shared letters
scenes.narration: An embedding model reads any string and returns a fixed-length list of floats — a point in a high-dimensional space where geometry encodes meaning. Texts used in similar contexts get vectors pointing the same way. To score closeness we use cosine similarity, the cosine of the angle between two vectors. That's why 'car' and 'automobile' land near each other even though they share no letters.

scenes.code:
import numpy as np

def cosine(a, b):
    a, b = np.array(a), np.array(b)
    return float(a @ b / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)))

a = [1.0, 0.0, 1.0]
b = [1.0, 0.0, 0.9]   # nearly same direction
c = [0.0, 1.0, 0.0]   # orthogonal -> unrelated
print(round(cosine(a, b), 3))  # ~0.997
print(round(cosine(a, c), 3))  # 0.0
scenes.heading: Cosine similarity in code
scenes.narration: Cosine similarity is just the dot product divided by the two vector lengths. Vectors pointing nearly the same way score close to one; perpendicular vectors score zero. Notice it divides out magnitude entirely — it cares only about direction, which is meaning, which is exactly what we want for text.

scenes.heading: Using embeddings correctly
items: Embed stored passages and queries with the SAME model
Vectors from different models aren't comparable
Dimensionality trades quality against memory and speed
scenes.narration: One rule matters most: embed your stored chunks and every incoming query with the same model, because vectors from different models live in different spaces and can't be compared. The model's dimensionality — say 384 versus 1536 — trades a little retrieval quality against memory and search cost, a decision that directly sizes the vector index you'll build next.

scenes.text: Embeddings turn meaning into geometry; cosine similarity ranks it. Same-meaning texts score near 1.0 even with zero shared words.
scenes.narration: Embeddings plus cosine similarity are the mathematical substrate beneath every dense retriever in RAG. They let search match on meaning rather than keywords — the single most important ingredient in retrieval quality.
